question: What is the main reason for offering family planning services through Primary Health Care?

options.A: To make services easy to reach close to home
options.B: To stop people from visiting urban hospitals
options.D: To remove the need for community health workers

explanation: Primary Health Care brings essential health services directly to the community level so everyone can access them easily. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T3#BMP224_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why is family planning best handled as part of routine Primary Health Care?

options.A: It stops patients from seeing traditional birth attendants
options.B: It removes the need for trained midwives in rural areas
options.C: It allows clients to get family planning along with other basic health visits
options.D: It exempts clinics from government supply chains

explanation: Integrating family planning into primary care lets clients receive contraceptive counseling and supplies during visits for other health needs. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T3#BMP224_U1_T3_h1)

question: How does proper spacing between pregnancies help protect a mother's health?

options.A: It guarantees higher birth weights for future babies
options.B: It prevents all forms of gestational diabetes
options.C: It gives the body time to recover its strength and nutrients
options.D: It removes the need for antenatal blood tests

explanation: Adequate intervals between pregnancies prevent maternal depletion by allowing nutrient stores and physical strength to rebuild. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T3#BMP224_U1_T3_h2)

question: A nursing mother brings her baby for routine immunization at the clinic. What is the best action for the midwife?

options.A: Ask her to book a separate appointment for next month
options.B: Tell her to wait until the child is one year old
options.C: Provide the immunization and also offer family planning counseling
options.D: Focus only on the baby's vaccines to keep things simple

explanation: Midwives seize every opportunity, such as an immunization visit, to provide comprehensive maternal health and family planning services together. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T3#BMP224_U1_T3_h2)

question: What happens in a 'one-stop shop' model of primary health care?

options.A: Community health workers operate completely on their own
options.B: Clients receive multiple related health services in the same location
options.C: Patients must visit different specialized hospitals for each test
options.D: Contraceptives are only distributed on designated market days

explanation: The one-stop shop model reduces waiting time and travel by offering various essential services under one roof. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T3#BMP224_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good practice in an integrated primary health care setting?

options.A: Offering family planning during routine postnatal visits
options.B: Establishing clear referral links between community workers and clinics
options.C: Using outreach teams to reach remote communities
options.D: Sending clients to distant tertiary facilities for basic pill refills

explanation: Basic contraceptive supplies like oral pills should be available at the primary care level, making distant referrals unnecessary for routine refills. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T3#BMP224_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which of these is a common supply challenge in primary health clinics?
explanation: Frequent stock-outs of commodities disrupt service delivery and turn clients away when they are ready to adopt a method. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T3#BMP224_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why is involving the local community important for family planning programs?

options.A: It helps clear up cultural myths and addresses partner concerns
options.B: It ensures clinics never run out of government funds
options.C: It allows clinics to stop keeping medical records
options.D: It replaces the need for skilled midwifery consultations

explanation: Involving community leaders and partners helps break down misconceptions and creates a supportive environment for women seeking care. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T3#BMP224_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is a main clinical duty of a midwife providing family planning in a primary health clinic?

options.A: Performing major surgeries outside the primary care scope
options.B: Deciding how many children a family should have
options.C: Importing foreign pharmaceutical drugs without approval
options.D: Assessing medical eligibility and giving supportive, respectful counseling

explanation: Midwives use clinical guidelines to ensure safe method selection while respecting client choices through supportive counseling. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T3#BMP224_U1_T3_h5)

question: A young woman visits the clinic feeling unsure about contraception due to rumors she heard. How should the midwife respond?

options.A: Prescribe the strongest method available to override her fears
options.B: Listen to her concerns patiently and provide accurate information
options.C: Refuse contraceptives until she brings her husband's written consent
options.D: Scold her for listening to gossip instead of professionals

explanation: Midwifery care involves respectful listening, clearing up myths with factual education, and supporting informed client choices. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T3#BMP224_U1_T3_h5)
